questions.q: Which organization created PyRIT?
questions.explanation: PyRIT (Python Risk Identification Tool) was built and open-sourced by Microsoft's AI Red Team.

questions.q: What is the correct pip install command for Garak?
questions.explanation: Garak installs with the simple command 'pip install garak'.

questions.q: In Garak's terminology, what is a 'probe'?
options: An attack module designed to trigger a specific vulnerability class
The adapter connecting to a target model
A scoring function for grading responses
questions.explanation: A probe is an attack module — e.g. dan, promptinject, encoding — each targeting a different vulnerability class.

questions.q: Which tool is specifically known for dynamic, multi-turn stress testing of RAG pipelines and chatbots, with a strong focus on hallucination detection?
questions.explanation: Giskard specializes in testing RAG chatbots for hallucination, factual consistency, and off-topic drift, not just jailbreaks.

questions.q: DeepTeam organizes its testing around what structure?
options: A matrix of vulnerability classes crossed with attack strategies
A YAML-only configuration with no code
questions.explanation: DeepTeam applies multiple attack strategies (jailbreaking, roleplay, encoding, etc.) against each vulnerability class (PII leakage, bias, excessive agency, etc.), producing a matrix of results.

questions.q: Which tool is best suited for wiring red teaming directly into a CI/CD pipeline using a YAML config file?
questions.explanation: Promptfoo is designed to run as a pipeline step from a promptfooconfig.yaml file, making it well suited to CI/CD gates.

questions.q: What is the Adversarial Robustness Toolbox (ART) primarily built by?
questions.explanation: ART (Adversarial Robustness Toolbox) is IBM's open-source library for evasion, poisoning, extraction, and inference attacks against ML models.

questions.q: CleverHans is best described as:
options: An enterprise CI/CD red teaming platform
A lightweight library of research-paper-accurate adversarial example algorithms (FGSM, PGD, etc.)
A network enumeration tool for AI infrastructure
questions.explanation: CleverHans focuses specifically on implementing published adversarial example generation algorithms in a lean, reference-accurate way.

questions.q: Which supporting tool would you use to intercept and modify HTTP requests sent to an LLM-backed API endpoint?
questions.explanation: Burp Suite is used to intercept, inspect, and modify API requests, letting you see exactly what's sent to an LLM endpoint and replay it with changes.

questions.q: What is CyberChef primarily used for in AI red teaming workflows?
options: Encoding and decoding payloads (Base64, ROT13, URL encoding, Unicode)
questions.explanation: CyberChef is a browser-based tool for encoding/decoding payloads, useful for building filter-evasion prompts like those tested by Garak's encoding probes.

questions.q: Which ports would be most relevant to check when running Nmap against AI infrastructure, based on this module?
questions.explanation: 11434 is Ollama's default port, 6333 is Qdrant's default port, and 9200 is Elasticsearch's default port — all common components of an AI stack.

questions.q: What technique does GCG (from the llm-attacks research) use to find adversarial suffixes?
questions.explanation: GCG uses Greedy Coordinate Gradient optimization to search for a suffix string that increases the likelihood of a harmful response, and these suffixes often transfer across models.

questions.q: PAIR (Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement) requires which type of access to the target model?
options: Physical access to the GPU server
questions.explanation: PAIR uses one LLM as an attacker to iteratively refine prompts against a target LLM using only its responses as feedback — no gradient or weight access is needed.

questions.q: How does TAP (Tree of Attacks with Pruning) improve on PAIR?
options: It branches multiple candidate prompts in a search tree and prunes unlikely branches
It only works against classic ML classifiers
It removes the need for any target model queries
questions.explanation: TAP explores multiple candidate jailbreak prompts as branches of a search tree, pruning branches an evaluator judges unlikely to succeed, generally making it more query-efficient than PAIR.

questions.q: What is JailbreakBench primarily used for?
options: Providing a standardized dataset and evaluation harness to benchmark jailbreak attacks and defenses
Scanning network ports on AI infrastructure
questions.explanation: JailbreakBench offers a shared dataset of harmful behaviors and a reproducible evaluation methodology so different attacks can be compared on equal footing.

questions.q: TextAttack was originally designed to attack what type of model?
options: Classic NLP classifiers (sentiment, spam, toxicity detectors)
questions.explanation: TextAttack was built for adversarial NLP against classifiers, which is directly relevant to attacking classifier-based guardrails placed in front of production LLMs.

questions.q: What does Rebuff primarily provide?
options: An attack framework for generating jailbreaks
A prompt-injection detection layer combining heuristics, an LLM judge, and canary tokens
questions.explanation: Rebuff is a defensive tool for detecting prompt injection, useful for a red teamer to understand what a defended target's guardrail stack might resemble.

questions.q: What advantage does AutoDAN offer over GCG-style attacks?
options: It requires no compute at all
It produces fluent, readable jailbreak prompts less likely to be flagged by perplexity-based filters
It only works on classifiers, not LLMs
It eliminates the need for any target access
questions.explanation: AutoDAN uses a genetic-algorithm-style search to evolve prompts that remain natural-sounding, unlike GCG's often unnatural/gibberish suffixes, helping evade filters that flag unusual text.

questions.q: According to the module, which category of tools generally requires white-box (model weight) access?
questions.explanation: GCG and AutoDAN are optimization-based attacks that typically require access to model weights or heavy compute, unlike black-box tools like PAIR and TAP.

questions.q: In a typical engagement flow described in this module, what comes right after infrastructure recon (Nmap/service discovery)?
options: A broad scan with Garak for fast baseline coverage
questions.explanation: The recommended flow runs Garak's broad scan early to get fast baseline coverage before moving to targeted, tool-specific deep-dives.

questions.q: Which tool would be most appropriate if your target has a classic spam-filter classifier sitting in front of an LLM, similar to labs in the AI Evasion module?
questions.explanation: ART and CleverHans are built for classic ML evasion attacks against classifiers like spam filters, directly extending the white-box/black-box evasion techniques covered earlier.

questions.q: Why does this module caution against relying purely on automated scanner output?
options: Because scanners can produce false positives and false negatives, just like any other security tool
Because scanners are illegal to use
Because scanners only work on closed-source models
questions.explanation: Automated tools automate techniques you should already understand from first principles; findings should still be validated manually since scanners can misjudge results in both directions.

questions.q: What is the primary reason PyRIT is well suited to enterprise environments?
options: It has the smallest probe library of any tool
It supports repeatable, auditable, multi-modal, chained attack pipelines
It only works with a single fixed CLI command
It cannot be integrated into other reporting pipelines
questions.explanation: PyRIT is a composable framework (targets, converters, orchestrators, scorers) designed for building repeatable and auditable red team pipelines, including multi-modal targets.
